points.title: 童年成长
points.description: 马丁·路德·金于1929年1月15日出生于亚特兰大，是牧师迈克尔·金和阿尔贝塔·威廉姆斯·金的儿子。他的家庭有着深厚的宗教传统，父亲和祖父都是埃比尼泽浸信会教堂的牧人。金在种族隔离的南方长大，亲身经历了种族歧视，但同时也受到了良好的教育。他从小展现出卓越的才能，15岁时进入莫尔豪斯学院学习社会学，19岁获得学士学位，成为当时最年轻的毕业生之一。
points.descriptionEn: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta on January 15, 1929, to Michael King and Alberta Williams King. His family had deep religious roots, with both his father and grandfather serving as pastors of Ebenezer Baptist Church. King grew up in the racially segregated South, experiencing discrimination firsthand while receiving quality education. He demonstrated exceptional talents early, entering Morehouse College at age 15 to study sociology and graduating with a bachelor's degree at 19, becoming one of the youngest graduates at the time.

points.title: 求学与思想形成
points.description: 金在波士顿大学攻读神学博士学位，同时也在哈佛大学学习。在此期间，他深入研究了甘地的非暴力抵抗哲学，并将其与美国基督教教义相结合，形成了自己独特的非暴力抗争理念。1953年，金与科雷塔·斯科特结婚，次年他成为蒙哥马利市德克斯塔大街浸信会教堂的牧师。这一时期的思想积累为他后来领导民权运动奠定了理论基础，使他成为将宗教信仰与社会正义紧密结合的领袖。
points.descriptionEn: King pursued his doctorate in theology at Boston University while also studying at Harvard. During this period, he deeply studied Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance, combining it with American Christian teachings to form his unique approach to nonviolent protest. In 1953, King married Coretta Scott, and the following year he became pastor of Dexter Avenue Baptist Church in Montgomery. This ideological groundwork prepared him to later lead the civil rights movement, becoming a leader who seamlessly integrated religious faith with social justice.

points.title: 蒙哥马利巴士抵制运动
points.description: 1955年12月，罗莎·帕克斯在蒙哥马利市拒绝给白人让座被捕，金随即领导了长达381天的蒙哥马利巴士抵制运动。他组织非暴力抗议，成立蒙哥马利改进协会，并运用演讲和布道动员社区。尽管面临暴力威胁和房屋被炸，金坚持抗争。1956年，最高法院裁定公交车上的种族隔离违宪，这场运动取得胜利。这一成功使金成为全国知名的民权领袖，也确立了非暴力抵抗作为民权运动主要策略的地位。
points.descriptionEn: In December 1955, Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery for refusing to give up her seat to a white passenger, prompting King to lead the 381-day Montgomery Bus Boycott. He organized nonviolent protests, formed the Montgomery Improvement Association, and mobilized the community through speeches and sermons. Despite facing violence threats and having his home bombed, King persisted. In 1956, the Supreme Court ruled that bus segregation was unconstitutional, securing victory for the movement. This success made King a national civil rights leader and established nonviolent resistance as the primary strategy of the civil rights movement.

points.title: 伯明翰运动与《我有一个梦想》
points.titleEn: Birmingham Campaign and 'I Have a Dream'
points.description: 1963年，金领导伯明翰运动，针对该市严厉的种族隔离法开展非暴力抗议。尽管面对警察使用警犬、高压水枪和暴力镇压，金坚持非暴力原则。同年8月，他在华盛顿大游行上发表《我有一个梦想》演讲，成为美国历史上最著名的演讲之一。1964年，金因领导非暴力抗争获得诺贝尔和平奖。1965年，他领导从塞尔马到蒙哥马利的游行，促使国会通过《选举权法》，这些行动极大地推动了民权立法进程。
points.descriptionEn: In 1963, King led the Birmingham Campaign against the city's strict segregation laws, conducting nonviolent protests despite facing police brutality with dogs, fire hoses, and violence. That August, he delivered his 'I Have a Dream' speech during the March on Washington, becoming one of the most famous speeches in American history. In 1964, King received the Nobel Peace Prize for leading nonviolent struggle. In 1965, he led the Selma to Montgomery marches, which led to the passage of the Voting Rights Act, significantly advancing civil rights legislation.

points.title: 最后岁月与遇刺
points.description: 1965年后，金将注意力转向经济正义和反贫困运动，并开始质疑越南战争。1968年，他前往孟菲斯支持当地环卫工人的罢工，要求改善工作条件和公平工资。4月3日，他在孟菲斯教堂发表了著名的《我已抵达山顶》演讲，预示着自己可能遭遇不测。次日，即1968年4月4日，金在孟菲斯洛林汽车旅馆的二楼阳台被暗杀，年仅39岁。他的遇刺引发了全国范围内的骚乱，但也促使国会通过《民权法案》和《住房法案》，巩固了民权运动的成果。
points.descriptionEn: After 1965, King shifted focus to economic justice and anti-poverty efforts, beginning to question the Vietnam War. In 1968, he traveled to Memphis to support local sanitation workers on strike, demanding better working conditions and fair wages. On April 3, he delivered his famous 'I've Been to the Mountaintop' speech, suggesting he might meet an untimely end. The next day, April 4, 1968, King was assassinated on the second-floor balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis at age 39. His assassination triggered riots nationwide but also led Congress to pass the Civil Rights Act and Fair Housing Act, solidifying the civil rights movement's achievements.

supporter.zh: 马丁·路德·金被广泛视为美国民权运动的伟大领袖和道德巨人。他通过非暴力抵抗策略，成功挑战了美国南方的种族隔离制度，推动了《民权法案》和《选举权法》的通过。金的思想不仅改变了美国社会，也影响了全球各地的和平运动。他倡导的'爱的社区'理念和'非暴力抵抗'哲学，为解决社会冲突提供了新的思路。金的精神遗产激励了后世无数社会正义运动，成为人类争取平等与尊严的象征。
supporter.en: Martin Luther King Jr. is widely regarded as a great leader and moral giant of the American civil rights movement. Through his strategy of nonviolent resistance, he successfully challenged racial segregation in the American South and led to the passage of the Civil Rights Act and Voting Rights Act. King's ideas not only transformed American society but also influenced peace movements worldwide. His philosophy of 'beloved community' and 'nonviolent resistance' provided new approaches to resolving social conflicts. King's legacy continues to inspire countless social justice movements, becoming a symbol of humanity's struggle for equality and dignity.

critic.zh: 批评者指出马丁·路德·金存在个人道德问题，包括婚外情和学术不端指控。一些民权运动内部人士认为他后期策略过于温和，未能解决经济不平等问题。此外，金对资本主义和军事干预的批评态度也引起争议。批评者还认为，他的非暴力策略在面对极端暴力时效果有限，且未能充分解决系统性种族主义问题。尽管如此，这些批评不应掩盖金在推动种族平等方面的历史性贡献，但确实反映了历史人物的复杂性和局限性。
critic.en: Critics point to Martin Luther King Jr.'s personal moral issues, including extramarital affairs and allegations of academic misconduct. Some civil rights movement insiders believed his later strategies were too moderate and failed to address economic inequality. Additionally, King's critical stance toward capitalism and military intervention was controversial. Critics also argue that his nonviolent strategy had limited effectiveness against extreme violence and failed to fully address systemic racism. Nevertheless, these criticisms should not overshadow King's historic contributions to advancing racial equality, but they do reflect the complexity and limitations of historical figures.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，马丁·路德·金被定义为美国民权运动的标志性人物和全球和平运动的象征。他的生平被广泛研究，成为美国历史的重要组成部分。金的思想和行动被纳入学校课程，他的演讲被反复引用，成为美国文化的一部分。然而，随着历史研究的深入，学界也呈现出更加复杂的图景，既肯定他的历史贡献，也探讨他的局限性和矛盾。在流行文化中，金的形象经历了从圣人到复杂历史人物的演变，反映了社会对历史人物认知的成熟过程。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Martin Luther King Jr. is defined as an iconic figure of the American civil rights movement and a symbol of global peace movements. His life has been widely studied, becoming an integral part of American history. King's ideas and actions are incorporated into school curricula, and his speeches are frequently quoted, becoming part of American culture. However, as historical research has deepened, scholarship has presented a more complex picture, both affirming his historical contributions and exploring his limitations and contradictions. In popular culture, King's image has evolved from saint to complex historical figure, reflecting the maturation of society's understanding of historical figures.

self.zh: 我有一个梦想，有一天这个国家将会站起来，真正实现其信条的真谛：'我们认为这些真理不言而喻，人人生而平等。'
self.en: I have a dream that one day this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed: 'We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.'

others.zh: 暴力只会产生更多暴力，而爱能治愈一切创伤。黑暗不能驱散黑暗，只有光明才能做到。仇恨不能驱散仇恨，只有爱才能做到。
others.en: Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that. Hate cannot drive out hate; only love can do that.
